findings.reason: Setter.ts:71 now calls transpose(date, Date), and index.ts:60 builds the setter with no context or reference, so options.in is never used. constructFrom then turns the system-zone instant back into the context type, which moves the wall clock by the offset difference. One correction to C1: priority 10 is the lowest, so the sort at index.ts:493-502 runs this setter last, not first. That means even full-date formats get shifted, as X1 says, and not only the fields the format leaves unset.
findings.claim: The timezone setter now ignores options.in and the reference date's type. It always copies the wall-clock time through the host's system zone, so parse results shift by the gap between the context zone's offset and the host's.
findings.evidence: The diff deletes the `context` constructor argument (`this.context = context || ((date) => constructFrom(reference, date))`) and replaces `transpose(date, this.context)` with `transpose(date, Date)`. In index.ts:395 the setter is now `new DateToSystemTimezoneSetter()`, so `options?.in` and `referenceDate` are no longer passed in. The setter has priority 10, the highest, so the sort at index.ts:493-502 runs it first, on `toDate(referenceDate, options?.in)`. transpose copies the wall-clock fields into a system-zone `Date`, and `constructFrom(date, …)` reads that timestamp back in the context zone. The reference wall-clock therefore moves by (context offset − system offset) before the parsers fill in only the tokens they parsed. With `in: tz("Asia/Singapore")` on a machine set to America/Los_Angeles, a reference of 20:00 on Apr 6 in Singapore becomes 11:00 on Apr 7, so `parse("10:00","HH:mm",ref,{in})` returns Apr 7. The same happens when a `UTCDate` reference is passed without `in`, which the old default context handled.

findings.reason: The timezone setter runs last (priority 10, sorted in descending order at index.ts:495), so it also shifts results that are fully specified. The Singapore context test at test.ts:2499-2507 expects 00:00+08:00 and would fail on any host whose offset isn't +08, and scripts/test/tzIANA.sh runs vitest across many zones. The existing tests can therefore catch it.
findings.claim: The context tests can't detect the regression because they use full-date formats.
findings.evidence: Both context tests and the UTCDate test (lines 2488-2527) parse "2018 hello world July 2nd" with "yyyy 'hello world' MMMM do". No test parses a partial format such as a time-only "HH:mm" with `{ in: tz(...) }` or a `UTCDate` reference, which is the input that would expose the system-zone round trip at Setter.ts:71.

findings.evidence: Setter.ts:1-2 swap the order of the `transpose` and `constructFrom` imports. The class is renamed from `DateTimezoneSetter` to `DateToSystemTimezoneSetter`. index.ts:506-508 replace `if (isNaN(+date)) return invalidDate();` with a braced block, and the logic is identical.
